# CVE-2026-135720 — FFmpeg: NULL pointer dereference in DASH LCEVC grouping

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135720 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/dashdec.c::dash_read_header` |
| **Affected** | 9.0 before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`fba9c09`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference) |
| **Impact** | When building LCEVC stream groups, `dash_read_header()` selected representations that had a dependency ID and associated streams but no `codecs` string. The builder dereferenced the missing codecs, crashing the demuxer. An attacker could supply a crafted MPD manifest to trigger it |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied DASH MPD manifest |
| **Trigger** | representation with `dependencyid` and associated streams but no `codecs` |

The vulnerable selection:

```c
// dashdec.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
if (!rep->dependencyid || !rep->nb_assoc_stream)
    continue;
// ... LCEVC group builder uses rep->codecs -> NULL deref
```

The fix adds the missing check:

```c
// fixed (commit fba9c09, verbatim in the lab)
if (!rep->dependencyid || !rep->codecs || !rep->nb_assoc_stream)
    continue;
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The selection predicate for LCEVC grouping required a dependency ID and
associated streams but omitted the `codecs` field. A crafted manifest could
satisfy the first two while leaving `codecs` NULL, and the group builder
dereferenced it. The fix adds `!rep->codecs` to the skip condition.

The C harness uses the selection guard from both commits with a crafted

# CVE-2026-135708 — FFmpeg: arbitrary file destruction through WHIP `Location` scheme

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135708 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/whip.c::exchange_sdp` |
| **Affected** | 8.0 before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`96994cb`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-20 (Improper Input Validation) |
| **Impact** | A malicious WHIP server could return a `file:` URL in the `Location` header. The muxer stored it as the session resource URL, and `dispose_session()` later opened it read-write with truncation, destroying arbitrary user-writable files. Other schemes could redirect requests to unintended protocols |
| **Vector** | malicious WHIP server responding to an SDP exchange |
| **Trigger** | `Location: file:///tmp/whip-victim` |

The vulnerable handling:

```c
// whip.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
if (ff_http_get_new_location(whip_uc)) {
    whip->whip_resource_url = av_strdup(ff_http_get_new_location(whip_uc));
    ...
}
// dispose_session() later opens whip_resource_url with O_TRUNC
```

The fix validates the protocol:

```c
// fixed (commit 96994cb, verbatim in the lab)
proto_name = avio_find_protocol_name(ff_http_get_new_location(whip_uc));
if (!proto_name || !av_strstart(proto_name, "http", NULL)) {
    av_log(whip, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Unsupported resource url %s\n", ...);
    ret = AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    goto end;
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The `Location` header from a server was trusted as a resource URL without
validating its scheme. Because teardown opens that URL read-write with
truncation, a `file:` scheme turned a protocol redirect into a destructive file
write. The fix restricts the resource URL to `http*` protocols.

# CVE-2026-135715 — FFmpeg: NULL pointer dereference in the AVIF muxer

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135715 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/movenc.c::mov_init` (AVIF muxer) |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`6fdfafa`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference) |
| **Impact** | When an AVIF output contained a second (alpha) stream with an unknown pixel format, `av_pix_fmt_desc_get()` returned NULL and `pixdesc->nb_components` dereferenced it, crashing the application. A primary stream with an unknown format was similarly unchecked |
| **Vector** | attacker-controlled input encoded to AVIF with an alpha stream |
| **Trigger** | AVIF output whose alpha stream has an unknown pixel format |

The vulnerable check:

```c
// movenc.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
const AVPixFmtDescriptor *pixdesc =
    av_pix_fmt_desc_get(s->streams[1]->codecpar->format);
if (pixdesc->nb_components != 1) { ... }   // pixdesc may be NULL
```

The fix validates both descriptors:

```c
// fixed (commit 6fdfafa, verbatim in the lab)
if (!av_pix_fmt_desc_get(s->streams[0]->codecpar->format)) {
    av_log(s, AV_LOG_ERROR, "AVIF output requires a known pixel format\n");
    return AVERROR(EINVAL);
}
...
if (!pixdesc || pixdesc->nb_components != 1) {
    av_log(s, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Second stream for AVIF (alpha) output must have exactly one plane\n");
    return AVERROR(EINVAL);
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

`av_pix_fmt_desc_get()` returns NULL for unknown or invalid pixel formats. The
muxer assumed a descriptor always existed and dereferenced it without a NULL
check. The fix checks the descriptor for both the primary and alpha streams
before reading `nb_components`.

# CVE-2026-135713 — FFmpeg: NULL pointer dereference in `mms_open()`

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135713 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/mmst.c::mms_open` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`94c3187`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-476 (NULL Pointer Dereference) |
| **Impact** | When a malicious MMS server sent an ASF header lacking a packet size or stream properties, `mms_open()` jumped to its failure label with the error variable still zero. The state was freed and `mms_open()` returned success; the client's first read then dereferenced the freed/NULL state, crashing it |
| **Vector** | malicious MMS server responding to an MMST connection |
| **Trigger** | ASF header with no packet size or stream count |

The vulnerable failure path:

```c
// mmst.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
if (!mms->asf_packet_len || !mms->stream_num)
    goto fail;                 // err is still 0 here
...
fail:
    mms_close(h);              // frees state
    return err;                // returns 0 = success
```

The fix sets an error before failing:

```c
// fixed (commit 94c3187, verbatim in the lab)
if (!mms->asf_packet_len || !mms->stream_num) {
    err = AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
    goto fail;
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The failure label returned a shared `err` variable. On the earlier success path
`err` was zero, and the malformed-header check jumped to `fail` without
assigning a new error. The function therefore freed its state and reported
success. The fix assigns `AVERROR_INVALIDDATA` so the caller stops before using
the invalid state.

# CVE-2026-135718 — FFmpeg: out-of-bounds read in DVD menu audio stream handling

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135718 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/dvdvideodec.c::dvdvideo_ifo_open` / `dvdvideo_audio_stream_add_all` |
| **Affected** | 7.0 before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`cc7f5bc`** — AISLE-2026-0111-00216 |
| **CWE** | CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read) |
| **Impact** | The title path rejected more than 8 audio streams, but the menu path did not. A crafted DVD image whose menu IFO declared more than 8 audio streams made `dvdvideo_audio_stream_add_all()` read past the fixed 8-entry `audio_control` array, crashing the demuxer |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied crafted DVD image |
| **Trigger** | menu IFO declaring 9 audio streams |

The vulnerable path:

```c
// dvdvideodec.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
// menu path: no check that nr_of_vmgm_audio_streams <= 8
for (int i = 0; i < nb_streams; i++)
    ... c->play_state.pgc->audio_control[i] ...   // 8-entry array
```

The fix validates the menu count at IFO open:

```c
// fixed (commit cc7f5bc, verbatim in the lab)
if ((!c->opt_menu_vts && c->vmg_ifo->vmgi_mat->nr_of_vmgm_audio_streams > 8) ||
    ( c->opt_menu_vts && c->vts_ifo->vtsi_mat->nr_of_vtsm_audio_streams > 8)) {
    av_log(s, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Menu has invalid headers (too many audio streams)\n");
    return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

Two code paths consumed the same fixed-size `audio_control` array. Only one
validated the stream count from the IFO metadata. Because the count is
attacker-controlled, the unvalidated menu path could index past the array. The
fix applies the same upper-bound check to both paths.

# CVE-2026-135706 — FFmpeg: heap buffer overflow in `modplug_read_header()`

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135706 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/libmodplug.c::modplug_read_header` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`edc96a2`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-122 (Heap Buffer Overflow) |
| **Impact** | The module input buffer was allocated with `max_size` instead of the actual number of bytes to read (`sz`). When a crafted module file left `max_size` at zero, `avio_read()` wrote `sz` bytes into a zero-byte allocation, corrupting the heap |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied module file passed to the libmodplug demuxer |
| **Trigger** | a module file that yields `max_size=0` with a nonzero read size |

The vulnerable allocation:

```c
// libmodplug.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
modplug->buf = av_malloc(modplug->max_size);   // may be 0
...
sz = avio_read(pb, modplug->buf, sz);          // writes sz bytes
```

The fix allocates the bytes actually read:

```c
// fixed (commit edc96a2, verbatim in the lab)
modplug->buf = av_malloc(sz);
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The allocation size and the read size came from different fields. `max_size` is
metadata that an attacker can leave unset, while `sz` is the number of bytes
`avio_read()` will actually write. Allocating the former and writing the latter
produces a heap overflow whenever `max_size < sz`. The fix uses `sz` for the
allocation.

# CVE-2026-135705 — FFmpeg: out-of-bounds read in `ff_h264_parse_framesize()`

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135705 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/rtpdec_h264.c::ff_h264_parse_framesize` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`e5fe2cb`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-125 (Out-of-bounds Read) |
| **Impact** | When parsing an SDP `a=framesize` attribute that lacks a height, `atoi(p + 1)` read past the line buffer. An attacker controlling an RTSP DESCRIBE response or a crafted `.sdp` file could crash clients or cause parsing of stale stack bytes |
| **Vector** | attacker-controlled RTSP DESCRIBE response or SDP file |
| **Trigger** | `a=framesize:96 320` (no `-height` suffix) |

The vulnerable parse:

```c
// rtpdec_h264.c — pre-fix (verbatim in the lab)
while (*p && *p != '-' && (dst - buf1) < sizeof(buf1) - 1)
    *dst++ = *p++;
*dst = '\0';
par->width  = atoi(buf1);
par->height = atoi(p + 1);   // p points at NUL when no '-' -> OOB read
```

The fix rejects malformed attributes:

```c
// fixed (commit e5fe2cb, verbatim in the lab)
*dst = '\0';
if (*p != '-')
    return;
par->width  = atoi(buf1);
par->height = atoi(p + 1);
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The copy loop terminates on a `-`, on the end of the string, or when the fixed
`buf1` fills. The code assumed a `-` was always present and unconditionally
parsed `p + 1` as the height. With a framesize attribute lacking a separator,
`p` points at the terminating NUL and `p + 1` is outside the line buffer. The
fix returns early when no separator was found.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135703 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c::asfrtp_parse_packet` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`f7fa69e`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-908 (Use of Uninitialized Resource) |
| **Impact** | The packet-length check only rejected a negative `FFMIN(cur_len, len-off)`. An oversized declared length passed, grew the reassembly buffer, but copied only the clamped number of bytes — leaving a gap of uninitialized heap that was emitted to the caller. A malicious RTSP server could leak heap contents |
| **Vector** | malicious RTSP server with an `x-asf-pf` payload |
| **Trigger** | declared packet length greater than remaining bytes |

The vulnerable check:

```c
// rtpdec_asf.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
if (FFMIN(cur_len, len - off) < 0) return -1;   // misses oversized cur_len
out_len += cur_len;                              // grows by full (oversized) value
av_reallocp(&asf->buf, out_len);
memcpy(asf->buf + prev_len, buf + off, FFMIN(cur_len, len - off));   // copies less
```

The fix rejects out-of-range lengths:

```c
// fixed (commit f7fa69e, verbatim in the lab)
if (cur_len < 0 || cur_len > len - off) return -1;
...
memcpy(asf->buf + prev_len, buf + off, cur_len);
```

---

## 1. Root cause

The validation used the clamped value while the allocation used the unclamped
one, so the buffer was larger than the data written into it. The fix validates
the true length before allocation, keeping allocation and copy in sync.

# CVE-2026-135721 — FFmpeg: infinite loop in VC-2 RTP muxing

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135721 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c::ff_rtp_send_vc2hq` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`3b7147d`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-835 (Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition) |
| **Impact** | A Dirac/VC-2 data unit declaring a next parse offset of zero made the parsing pointer never advance, so the muxing loop ran forever. Crafted video remuxed to RTP could hang the process, consuming CPU indefinitely |
| **Vector** | attacker-supplied Dirac/VC-2 video remuxed to RTP |
| **Trigger** | data unit with `unit_size == 0` |

The vulnerable loop:

```c
// rtpenc_vc2hq.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
while (unit < end) {
    unit_size = AV_RB32(&unit[5]);     // can be 0
    ...
    unit += unit_size;                 // never advances when 0
}
```

The fix bounds the loop and rejects short units:

```c
// fixed (commit 3b7147d, verbatim logic in the lab)
while (end - unit >= DIRAC_DATA_UNIT_HEADER_SIZE) {
    unit_size = AV_RB32(&unit[5]);
    if (unit_size < DIRAC_DATA_UNIT_HEADER_SIZE || unit_size > end - unit)
        break;
    ...
}
```

## 1. Root cause

The loop condition and unit-size validation did not guarantee forward progress.
A zero or undersized unit size left the pointer stationary. The fix requires a
full header of remaining bytes and rejects unit sizes below the header size.

# CVE-2026-135709 — FFmpeg: OOB write in OGG page buffering

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Research status: validated](https://img.shields.io/badge/research-validated%20differential-success.svg)](#5-expected-results)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **CVE** | CVE-2026-135709 |
| **Component** | FFmpeg — `libavformat/oggenc.c::ogg_buffer_page` |
| **Affected** | before 9.1 |
| **Fixed in** | **`f75923e`** |
| **CWE** | CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) |
| **Impact** | When the page-list allocation failed, `ogg_buffer_page()` returned without resetting the current page, which remained full. The next `ogg_buffer_data()` call then wrote into the stale full page with an invalid length, causing an out-of-bounds write |
| **Vector** | conditions that make page allocation fail during OGG muxing |
| **Trigger** | page-list allocation failure followed by a data write |

The vulnerable failure path:

```c
// oggenc.c — pre-fix (behavior in the lab)
OGGPageList *l = av_mallocz(sizeof(*l));
if (!l)
    return AVERROR(ENOMEM);   // current page left full/stale
```

The fix resets the page:

```c
// fixed (commit f75923e, verbatim in the lab)
if (!l) {
    ogg_reset_cur_page(oggstream);
    return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
}
```

---

## 1. Root cause

An error path returned without restoring the muxer's page state. The stale full

# `drupal-installer-scanner`

Detection-only triage for `CVE-2026-132165`, the `Drupal core` installer flaw (`SA-CORE-2026-017`) that lets an unauthenticated visitor try to reinstall a site that is already installed — and take it over. `Drupal` disclosed it on `18 Nov 2026`, rated it `Highly critical 20/25`, and later added that it was exploited on live sites as early as `19 Nov 2026 19:00 UTC`. `CISA` added it to its `Known Exploited Vulnerabilities` catalog on `24 Nov 2026`, due `27 Nov 2026`. Grades your core version against the fixed releases, reads the version your site already discloses, and probes `/core/install.php` with one plain `GET` to see whether the installer answers "already installed" or serves an install form. Nothing here sends a payload, submits a form, or `POST`s anything.

## `What it checks`

* `CVE-2026-132165` — `Drupal core` ships with `core/install.php`, and it stays on the site after installation. Under specific conditions, an anonymous visitor can use that installer to try to reinstall a finished site, which can lead to site takeover or remote code execution. `CVSS 3.1 9.8` (`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`) per `Tenable`, citing `Mitre`/`NVD`; a `CVSS 4.0` score of `9.2` is also in circulation, and `NVD` had not published a record of its own at the time of writing, so the `9.8` is the `Tenable` figure and the `9.2` is the second opinion — both agree it is critical, they disagree on the decimal. `CWE-94` (code injection) per the bulletin; some trackers also map it to `CWE-284` / `CWE-502`. Found by `Anthropic's OSS Scanner` (`ANT-2026-GMRPK0BU`).

Fixed versions, per the vendor advisory `SA-CORE-2026-017` (primary source):

| `Branch` | `Upgrade to` |
| --- | --- |
| `Drupal 10.6.x` | `10.6.22` (or later) |
| `Drupal 11.3.x` | `11.3.22` (or later) |
| `Drupal 11.4.x` | `11.4.13` (or later) |

`Drupal 11.2.x` and below, `10.5.x` and below, and `Drupal 8` and `9` are end of life and get no fix on those branches. `Drupal 11.5 beta` and `12.0` are listed as affected in the `16 November` PSA with no fixed release on those lines yet — this scanner grades them vulnerable and says so.

* The companion flaw, same releases, same fix. `CVE-2026-132166` (`SA-CORE-2026-018`, `Moderately critical 14/25`) is a gadget chain in `Drupal core` classes. It is not directly exploitable — it needs a separate bug that unserializes attacker input, and administrator access — so this scanner flags it in the same verdict rather than pretending it is a separate problem.

If you cannot update yet, block the installer. The advisory says to deny `/core/install.php` at the web server, with a prefix rule, not an exact-match rule — an exact-match rule lets `/core/install.php/foo` through. Keeping the web server from writing to or changing permissions on `settings.php` mitigates some, but not all, exploit paths.

## `Usage`

```bash
# grade a version string
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12"
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.13"

# a live site: public reads only — CHANGELOG.txt, X-Generator, one GET of /core/install.php
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --url https://example.com

# the box that runs the site (web root or project root)
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --local-dir /var/www/html

# hunt the access logs for installer requests (POSTs are attack probes)
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12" --access-log /var/log/nginx/access.log

# hunt a Drupal tree for PHP files under sites/*/files (uploaded shells)
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12" --ioc-dir /var/www/html

# a whole fleet at once
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --inventory-json fleet.json

# machine output / the fixed-version table
python3 drupal_installer_scanner.py --version "11.4.12" --json
        ```
